title: Cross-channel attribution: what it shows and misses

facts.fact: Google's documentation states that data-driven attribution is now the default for most conversion actions in Google Ads.
facts.quote: says data-driven attribution is now the default for most conversion actions.

facts.fact: Google Analytics 4's Attribution reports offer three models: data-driven attribution and two last-click models.
facts.quote: lists three models in its Attribution reports: data-driven attribution and two last-click models.

facts.fact: In one geo holdout on streaming TV cited by the page from Measured's incrementality research, roughly half of the conversions the ad platform had claimed were actually incremental.
facts.quote: roughly half of the conversions the ad platform had claimed were actually incremental

facts.fact: The page states that an incrementality test typically takes several weeks, long enough to cover the lag between seeing an ad and buying.
facts.quote: a test typically takes several weeks

facts.fact: The page says the platform-report reconciliation check described in its process takes about ten minutes for one month of data.
facts.quote: You can check this in about ten minutes:

facts.fact: The page states that most streaming platforms support geographic targeting exclusions, which makes streaming TV suitable for geo incrementality tests.
facts.quote: Streaming TV suits this because most streaming platforms support geographic targeting exclusions.

facts.fact: Last-touch attribution gives all credit to the final click or view before conversion, and the page says it overvalues the final touchpoint and ignores everything that came before it.
facts.quote: even though it overvalues the final touchpoint and ignores everything that came before it

facts.fact: The page states that multi-touch and data-driven attribution need user-level tracking and therefore cannot follow linear TV or other media they cannot tie to a person.
facts.quote: Needs user-level tracking, so it can’t follow linear TV or other media it can’t tie to a person

facts.fact: The page states that in an incrementality test, the difference in sales between the treatment and holdout groups is the lift the ads caused.
facts.quote: The difference in sales between the treatment and holdout groups is the lift the ads caused.

facts.fact: The page explains that each ad platform's dashboard counts the conversions its own ads touched, using its own conversion definition and attribution window, so platform totals can overlap.
facts.quote: Each counts the conversions its ads touched, using its own conversion definition and attribution window.
